films.title: Dyatlov Pass
films.subtitle: What Really Happened to the Nine Hikers?
films.description: RELEASED v1.1.0 (period-photo edition) — the cold open now uses the real 1959 archival photograph of the abandoned tent (Public domain, credited) acquired through the studio's imgacq pipeline (discovery → validated download → provenance ledger → human inspection → staged slot). 15:10, 1920x1080, -16.0 LUFS, deterministic re-render, SRT byte-identical to v1.0.0. Nine experienced winter hikers died on a Soviet slope in February 1959 after cutting their way out of their own tent; the film tests every theory against the documented evidence and follows the 2021 ETH Zurich slab-avalanche model. Evidence-first; theories labelled; nothing invented.

films.title: The Isdal Woman
films.subtitle: The Woman Who Erased Her Own Identity
films.description: RELEASED v2.2.0 (edge-tts re-voiced edition) — full cinematic rebuild at 1920x1080p24 with narration by Microsoft edge-tts neural voice (en-US-GuyNeural). In November 1970, a burned body was found in Norway's Isdalen valley. Her labels were cut off, her names were false, and fifty-five years later her identity remains unknown. 16:28 evidence-first film + 4 vertical shorts. Photo-first engine: 11 credited real photographs, Ken Burns motion, film grain, crossfades. Every claim sourced; theories labelled; nothing invented.

films.title: Zodiac
films.subtitle: The Ciphers That Refused to Die
films.description: RELEASED v1.0.0 — full 15:52 investigative documentary at 1920x1080p24, narration by Microsoft edge-tts (en-US-GuyNeural). The documented record: four confirmed attacks (5 murdered, 2 survivors), ~20 letters, the 408 cipher solved in 1969 (FBI-corroborated), the 340 cipher solved December 2020 (FBI-confirmed), the unsolved Z13/Z32, the partial print and partial DNA, and every suspect theory labelled as theory. 12 credited real photographs; cipher grids and newspapers are labelled reconstructions; evidence-first, nothing invented.

films.title: The Ostrich, Engraved
films.subtitle: One plate, one build — a copperplate natural-history short
films.description: RELEASED v1.0.0 — the lost copperplate-engraving short restored from its preserved method. A 62.7-second museum science-card film: the burin cuts the ostrich onto raw copper, the proof is pulled, four magnified roundels carry the facts (the largest eye of any land animal; a brain smaller than either eye; two toes only; the largest egg of any living bird), the washes hand-colour the print, the plate signs itself. 88 BPM score in code, D minor to D major at the wash; house edge-tts narration. Every fact established.
